candidates.description: VoxMel: Wavelet-Factorized Autoregressive Mel-Spectrogram Modeling for Zero-Shot Speech Synthesis
candidates.readme_excerpt:
VoxMel: Wavelet-Factorized Autoregressive Mel-Spectrogram Modeling for Zero-Shot Speech Synthesis

English | 中文 | 日語 | 한국어

Technical Report (coming soon) | Project Page | GitHub | Hugging Face

**VoxMel** is a tokenizer-free continuous autoregressive text-to-speech (TTS) framework that directly models mel-spectrograms through a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform. A language-model backbone with a flow-matching head generates **Coarse-Mel** autoregressively; two non-autoregressive residual tiers recover temporal and frequency details without feeding them back into the autoregressive history. A separate Vocos vocoder converts the reconstructed mel-spectrogram into speech. Trained on **100K hours of Emilia**, VoxMel is evaluated on English and Chinese zero-shot voice cloning. The **0.6B** supervised model achieves **1.51% WER / 0.738 SIM** on Seed-TTS-eval test-en; frozen-head GRPO improves this to **1.15% WER / 0.753 SIM**. See [Evaluation](#-evaluation) for comparisons and the evaluation protocol. ### ✨ Highlights - **Direct mel modeling** — No learned acoustic tokenizer or compressed acoustic latent space; the text frontend uses the Qwen2.5 tokenizer. - **Exactly invertible decomposition** — Frequency and temporal Haar splits preserve all mel coefficients. Exact invertibility applies to the transform, rather than guaranteeing lossless generated audio or vocoder reconstruction. - **Coarse-only autoregression** — Generate Coarse-Mel first, then the temporal residual and frequency residual in dependency order. candidates.readme_excerpt:
# AnySpeechRecognizer

AnySpeechRecognizer is a Swift package that implements Apple's modern Speech API
with a choice of recognition engine.
Code written for `SpeechAnalyzer`, `SpeechTranscriber`, `DictationTranscriber`,
`SpeechDetector`, and `AssetInventory` builds against this package
when you change the import statement:

```diff
- import Speech
+ import AnySpeechRecognizer
```

The default backend is Apple's Speech framework.
The package also has its own runtime for NVIDIA's
[Parakeet TDT](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3) models on Core ML,
with file and live input, volatile results, and word timing.
To use it, pass a model instead of a locale when you create the transcriber:

```diff
  let transcriber = SpeechTranscriber(
-     locale: locale,
+     model: ParakeetSpeechModel(variant: .v3),
      transcriptionOptions: [],
      reportingOptions: [.volatileResults],
      attributeOptions: [.audioTimeRange]
  )
```

Asset installation, analysis, and results use the same API for both backends.
As a package extension, `SpeakerDiarizer` identifies who speaks when
with NVIDIA's Streaming Sortformer model, on the same timeline as the transcriber.
The package does not implement the older `SFSpeechRecognizer` API.

## Requirements

- Swift 6.2 or later
- macOS 26 or later, or iOS 26 or later
- Apple silicon for the Parakeet and Sortformer models

## Installation

Add the package to your `Package.swift`:

```swift
.package(url: "https://github.com/mattt/AnySpeechRecognizer", from: "0.1.0")
```

The package uses
[swift-huggingface](https://github.com/huggingface/swift-huggingface)
to download and cache model files.

## Usage

### Transcribe a file

Resolve a locale, install assets explicitly,
and read results while the analyzer reads the file:

```swift
import AVFoundation
import AnySpeechRecognizer

func transcribe(_ url: URL) async throws -> AttributedString {
    guard let locale = await SpeechTranscriber.supportedLocale(
        equivalentTo: Locale(identifier: "en-US")
    ) else {
        throw SpeechRecognitionError.unsupportedLanguage("English is unavailable.")
    }
    let transcriber = SpeechTranscriber(

        reportingOptions: [],
        attributeOptions: [.audioTimeRange]
    )

    ) {
        try await request.downloadAndInstall()
    }

Picture your next scene: you type the brief, the copilot inspects the viewport, builds the pedestal, camera and lights, assigns the materials, and answers with a finished snapshot on the Studio task board.

## Why

Building in Blender still means menus, mouse miles and copy-pasted Python snippets—hours of mechanical work between you and the idea. blender-ai-copilot-studio puts a scene-aware AI copilot inside Blender: it reads your scene first, then carries out multi-step briefs as supervised tool calls with approvals, cancellation and named undo. You keep creating in Blender and let plain language handle the repetitive parts—so a full layout takes one sentence instead of an afternoon.

## Without / With

| Without | With |
|---|---|
